summary: Practise risk registers, partner assessments and residual-risk decisions for humanitarian projects. Explore the five-day course outline.
lede: Humanitarian project risk management helps project managers, programme staff and risk practitioners assess changing threats and make documented choices during design and delivery. It involves analysing context and stakeholders, maintaining risk registers and matrices, assigning mitigation actions, and reviewing protection, partner capacity and residual risk so teams can weigh controls against assistance-delivery needs.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for intermediate-level professionals who make or support risk decisions across humanitarian project design and delivery. It suits practitioners who need to connect changing context, affected people’s perspectives, partner capacity and project controls.
audience: Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning Officers
prerequisites: Designed for professionals with prior experience in humanitarian project or programme delivery, risk review or compliance work. You should be familiar with project plans and implementation responsibilities. No programming is required; bring a laptop with Excel or equivalent spreadsheet software for risk registers and action tracking.
